answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring signal transit across a grid where every agent must reach a specific jetty to certify their position. An issuer assigns spatial coordinates as a walnut anchor, and each receipt proves occupancy. A verifier reproduces failure by re-running logs; any latency drift exceeding the umber noise threshold triggers a penalty. Honest nodes pay linear travel costs, while 1,000 fakes incur unsustainable signal congestion without relay help.
